node_definition.done_when:
The lead rejected judging the Jev picker by agreement with deterministic routing, because there is no evidence deterministic routing was correct. Judge the picker by the outcomes of its own decisions instead. Build that measurement as Python, so that the CLI and agents read the same facts.

1. Add a module, for example reckon/crew/picker/outcomes.py, that reads ledger rows carrying picker_selection across every mounted project (reckon.flight.mounted_project_docs, then each project's docs/state/(project name)/runs), filtered by an optional since timestamp and project. It derives:
 (a) Mechanics: the count of each action (route, hold, fallback, refuse); fallback reasons grouped by kind (timeout, jev-error, input errors); and pick latency_ms p50 and p90, overall and per project.
 (b) Outcomes of routed runs, grouped by chosen backend × role × spec_level (and by the node's risk if the row records it): the count, the success rate, the review-score median, the repair or resume count, and wall_seconds against the run-time profile's p50 for that shape. Define success explicitly, from the row's recorded outcome and gate fields, and state the rule in the output and the docstring.
 (c) Calibration: picks bucketed by confidence (below 0.5, 0.5–0.7, 0.7–0.85, 0.85 and above), with the success rate per bucket.
 (d) Metered spend: routed codex runs with the burn_multiple and pace_allowance that were offered at pick time; and, among picks where a codex candidate was offered, the share that went to codex at each burn level.
 (e) Holds. A held dispatch creates no run, so first check whether picker holds are recorded anywhere durable (for example the ledger's holds list). If they are not, record each picker hold durably at dispatch: run_id-free, with the node, project, time, confidence and reasons. Then report the hold count and whether the same node was later dispatched, where, and how that run fared.
2. Expose it as `reckon crew pick --outcomes [--since ISO] [--project P|--all-projects]` on the existing pick verb, emitting JSON that names every rule it applied. Add the flag's line to the pick entry in skills/reckon-build/SKILL.md only if that keeps tests/test_skill_contracts.py green (its expected-flags table, and its FIXED_READ_SET_TOKEN_BUDGET, may need the same small, minimal edits a previous node made, with the reason recorded).
3. Run it on the live ledgers since 2026-10-03T03:00Z (the switch), and publish the first reading, with every figure from tool output, in docs/evidence/fragments/one-typesafe-model-picker/picker-outcomes.html, with one figure: success rate by confidence bucket, with counts.

Tests in tests/test_picker_outcomes.py: build rows on a temp fixture with known outcomes and assert each derived figure, including the success rule, the calibration buckets, fallback grouping and hold recording, with an empty ledger and with malformed rows.

Gate: that file, tests/test_picker*.py, tests/test_skill_contracts.py and tests/test_crew_help_names_its_state.py. Run with the main checkout's .venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -n 8 in the FOREGROUND, with one log for base and one for head under the run directory, each ending in an EXIT line, judged by delta. reckon/crew/dispatch.py may be edited only to record holds, in the hold path, and nowhere else.
